speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I was having a cup of tea with hon Members at a table in the Members' Room.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: From the corner of my eye, I saw the Prime Minister entering the room and walking to us.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I said to my Parliamentary colleagues, in what I thought was an undertone, "Boss coming." After sitting down beside me, the Prime Minister turned to me and said, "I am not your boss." Thinking back, what the Prime Minister said profoundly captures the essence of the relationship between backbencher Members of Parliament (MPs) of the governing party and the political office holders.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As MPs of the governing party, we are not subordinates of the Ministers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: On the contrary, we have an important responsibility in scrutinising Government action and holding Ministers to account.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It is worth reminding ourselves that structurally, we are independent and free to express our thoughts in this House on matters that affect our constituents and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The principle of collective responsibility that binds the Cabinet does not extend to backbenchers of the governing party.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Of course, we have to abide by the Whip in voting according to the party platform.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: That is a separate matter involving party discipline and that applies to Opposition MPs too.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: My party colleagues and I in the backbench take this responsibility of holding Ministers to account seriously.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We engage Ministers through correspondence, face-to-face meetings and party caucuses.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We also do this through the Parliamentary processes, particularly by filing Parliamentary Questions and Motions.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This provides an added advantage – the sunlight of scrutiny of Government action – something hon Members know I have advocated for in this House not too long ago.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There is therefore a healthy tension in the relationship between us.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: On one hand, as MPs, we accord the Minister, his office and Ministry with respect.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: At the same time, the Minister takes our feedback seriously.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He knows that we will not hesitate to pursue issues important to our constituents and fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is how we prevent groupthink and the creation of echo chambers within the PAP.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In short, we have backbone, we are independent, we strive to keep the Ministers on the straight and narrow.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: At the same time, we are fully responsible and accountable for our actions too.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It provides essential primary school services to residents of Bukit Batok Single Member Constituency (SMC) and nearby constituencies.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Over more than three and a half decades, the school forged a close relationship with the Bukit Batok community.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Senior community leaders and residents of Bukit Batok as well as former students serve in the School Advisory Committee (SAC).

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The community, through the SAC and grassroots organisations, gives tangible support to BVPS in the form of raising funds for the school's development plans, helping children from less privileged backgrounds and providing opportunities to school students to develop their character by participating in community assignments.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Its importance became more accentuated after the recent completion of BTO projects in its vicinity between 2017 and 2018.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: They are Skyline I and II and SkyPeak.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The majority of these units are occupied by young couples and families with young children.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Under the header "Feel the Pulse of Vibrant Living", it is stated as follows, "Parents with school-going children will be delighted to find a good range of educational institutions in close proximity.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These include Bukit View Primary." I now go to the brochure advertising SkyPeak @ Bukit Batok.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Under the header "Where Conveniences Abound", it is stated that "schools in the vicinity include Bukit View Primary." BVPS also provided a photo for the brochure and was accredited for it.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is to facilitate major upgrading works at the school.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This caused some concern amongst parents who had to make transport arrangements to shuttle their children to and fro the new site.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Thankfully, with understanding from all sides concerned and arrangements such as school bus services at an attractive rate, the concerns were largely addressed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In July 2019, MOE informed the students and parents of BVPS that as more time was required to enhance the design of the upgrading to allow for more efficient use of space and better traffic management, the BVPS upgrading plan would be delayed by one year.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As a result, the move was postponed to January 2021 instead.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The school was to return to the site by December 2022.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Around a year later, in 2020, the students and parents were told that the move will be delayed further by one year from January 2021 to January 2022 instead.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: By that time, the former Shuqun Secondary School site, which BVPS was supposed to move into, was used as a Regional Screening Centre.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It remains as a Joint Testing and Vaccination Centre.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In a separate development, going back to around 2020, PCF Sparkletots @ SkyPeak, which is located near BVPS, was told that BVPS was to be designated as an MOE kindergarten from 1 January 2024.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: PCF was asked to partner the MOE Kindergarten at BVPS.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: PCF expanded its infant care and childcare facilities so that it can provide a pipeline for enrolment at the MOE Kindergarten at BVPS.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The expansion works were completed in or around 2021.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I wish to add that news about the designation of BVPS as the site of an MOE Kindergarten percolated into the community.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I personally spoke to two persons, Mdm Wendy Koh and Mr Dennis Chua, both residing at SkyPeak, on Monday this week.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: They told me that they were aware of this matter and had welcomed this development.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I spoke to BVPS’ School Advisory Committee (SAC) Chairman, Mr Tommi Toh; Vice-Chairman, Mr Sonny Yuen as well as Mr Don Tay, an SAC member last week.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: They informed that the school told them the news about one hour before MOE went public.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Mr Tommi Toh, an old boy of the school who also got his two daughters to attend the same school, expressed that he was “shocked” by the decision.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He felt that the SAC should have been consulted and its views solicited as a key stakeholder.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Mr Don Tay felt the same way and informed that he does not fault the principal of the school as she told him she too got to know of the decision without much prior notice.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I learnt about the matter on the same day of the announcement.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: So, my first question to the hon Minister is simply this.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Against the backdrop of the facts I outlined, why was there no consultation?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We are not dealing with an urgent matter that requires decisive action such as defending the Singapore dollar.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We are not also dealing with a market sensitive matter such as increasing stamp duty when buying properties.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: On the contrary, we are dealing with a decision to withdraw essential educational services from a neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Surely, there should be consultation amongst the affected residents, parents, SAC members and other stakeholders?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This was the point that several residents made to me.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Mr Jeremy Ng and his wife are a young couple.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: They also have a five-year-old nephew whom they are taking care of.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Their decision to purchase a unit at SkyPeak was influenced by the fact that there will be primary school services within walking distance.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This was what was represented in the HDB brochures.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: One of the schools in the vicinity, Keming Primary School, is perpetually full by Phase 2C.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Hence BVPS provides an important assurance that they will be able to secure a primary school place within walking distance from their home.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Another person, Mdm Linda Chong, also a SkyPeak resident, has two children, aged 19 months and five years respectively.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Her elder child was born in the same year that she moved into SkyPeak; 2018.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She is naturally concerned about the lack of MOE Kindergarten and primary school facilities within walking distance once BVPS moves out.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In fact, I wonder if the hon Minister’s attention was drawn to the representations made in the HDB brochures, ECDA’s communication about PCF @ Sparkletots partnering the MOE Kindergarten at BVPS as well as prior communication to the parents at the time when the decision to relocate BVPS was made?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: If not, this is precisely why a consultation with stakeholders would have helped.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I appreciate that there are differences in the details of the two moves, but both are relocations of schools which are important community nodes.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: My second question is why were there so many flip-flops on what to do with BVPS within a short span of time even accounting for the effect of the pandemic?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Respectfully, it does not give people confidence that MOE is on top of the matter and has made proper plans for the future.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Such relocations, when not given proper notice, causes real hardship to families.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This point was raised to me by Mr Nazri, whom I met at a house visit just last week.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The elder child, a daughter, is in Primary 1 at BVPS.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: They had originally attempted to get a place for her at Princess Elizabeth Primary School (PEPS).

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The hon Minister would know that the local demand for Primary 1 places at PEPS had shot up significantly after the completion of housing developments in a neighbouring constituency.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It is not surprising therefore that they failed to be balloted a place at PEPS even though they were living close by.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: They therefore enrolled her in BVPS which was about 1.5 kilometres away.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Fortunately, Mrs Nazri’s mother is living nearby and therefore is able to take care of his daughter whilst he and his wife are working.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Both Mr and Mrs Nazri are concerned that the move will further inconvenience them.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In this regard, I highlight again that within the past five years, there are three completed BTO developments in Bukit Batok SMC.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This shows there is and continues to be demand for Primary 1 places in this constituency.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I say all this, not because I disagree with the decision per se, or as a petulant response to a lack of consultation.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: If I, the SAC members, affected residents and parents had nothing of value to add, if a discussion would have yielded no additional insights, if there were no people who acted in reliance of certain facts which are now changed, if all these were the case, it is perfectly fine that we learn of this ex post facto.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I wonder though whether this is the position that the hon Minister takes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Many of you also share useful feedback to MOE on school-related matters which we take seriously and try our best to address.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MOE regularly reviews the demand and supply trends for school places at the national and regional levels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our school planning takes into account current and projected populations, as well as planned housing programmes to ensure that there are sufficient school places to meet the needs of school-going children in each area.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Because of parental preferences, some schools may see demand consistently exceeding the available vacancies, whereas there could be some schools in the same area which have vacancies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: On the whole, our Primary 1 admission exercise has consistently enabled about 98% of Singaporean children to get into a Primary school of their choice or within two kilometres of their residence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Like other towns, MOE planned school places in Bukit Batok on the basis of current and known housing developments and these are updated regularly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Demand for school places in Bukit Batok East where BVPS is currently located has been falling and will continue to fall as the estate matures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: On the other hand, Bukit Batok West has seen a steadily growing demand for school places as a result of several more new BTOs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: And for the whole of Bukit Batok, the total Primary 1 demand in Bukit Batok remains roughly the same over the medium to long term.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This means that Bukit Batok as a whole, for this area, MOE does not need more new primary schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: But we have to take a careful look at where they are located as the weight of demand shifts from Bukit Batok East to Bukit Batok West and the new Tengah Town.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As such, in our most recent review in 2021, we re-assessed our earlier decision to upgrade BVPS at its current location in Bukit Batok East.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Murali has raised concerns over possible localised shortage of Primary 1 places when BVPS moves out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In particular, he is concerned over the demand from recent BTO projects namely Skyline, Sky Peak and Sky Vista.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have estimated that these BTOs would not reverse the overall declining demand in Bukit Batok East due to the ageing profile of the other households in the area.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: When BVPS relocates to its new campus, there will be sufficient school places for Mr Murali’s residents, in two other primary schools – Keming Primary School, Lianhua Primary School – and other nearby schools like Dazhong Primary School and St Anthony’s Primary School.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: There are altogether six primary schools in Bukit Batok.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For the benefit of Members in the Chamber who are not familiar with the area, BVPS, Keming Primary School and Lianhua Primary School are within close proximity of one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: So, what we are essentially planning to do is relocate one of them from Bukit Batok East to Bukit Batok West where there will be higher demand for primary school places in the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MOE has done similar relocations over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: One recent example is in 2022, for Angsana Primary School, where all students moved to a new campus also about two kilometres away within Tampines town.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Using the “lift and shift” method, we kept the school intact, ensured all students benefited from the new facilities at the new campus and provided a sense of continuity for the students and teachers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: BVPS will adopt this similar approach, which is the preferred approach, when the relocation is over a relatively short distance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: All of BVPS’ students currently in Primary 3 and above would not be affected by the move.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For the current Primary 1 and Primary 2 students, MOE has consulted the school leaders on measures to minimise inconvenience to those affected by the relocation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: About 40% of the current Primary 1 and 2 students live in Bukit Batok West.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: BVPS’ subsequent new Primary 1 cohorts would likely have even higher proportions staying in Bukit Batok West.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For current BVPS students who live in Bukit Batok East, the school will consider providing bus shuttle service for those who stay within walking distance from its current campus if there is sufficient demand.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I hope the affected parents will give the school time and their support to work through these measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Where necessary, MOE will also give additional resources to the school leaders to make the transition arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We appreciate that any change of plans, including for BVPS, could be disruptive and maybe even disappointing to some quarters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In addition, for the local community and for Mr Murali, MOE fully understands that BVPS has been a part of the community for decades.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We would like to assure Mr Murali that MOE does not take lightly a relocation decision unless we are convinced this is in the best interest of our current and future students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Murali has asked MOE why he was not informed early of MOE’s change of plan for BVPS after our internal review.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In the case of the relocation of ACS (Primary) to Tengah, selected members of their Board of Governors had to be consulted as it involved land owned by the Methodist Church.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Once MOE has arrived at a decision, we will strive to put in transition arrangements as early and as thoroughly as possible to mitigate any local impact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For the case of BVPS, as with other relocations, MOE would communicate the decision and considerations to the local advisor at the appropriate opportunity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Murali also raised concerns over how the change in plan for a possible MOE Kindergarten (MK) at BVPS would affect residents in Bukit Batok SMC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We would also like to thank Mr Murali for his sincere efforts to regularly communicate with MOE and representing the interests of the residents in his area.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: If the 30 minutes is not up, a Member can seek clarification on the reply.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: That being so, I shall put the question.
